items.title: Bill Watrous interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 26, 1999
items.q: He would open it up and let guys play. Let Eddie Daniels play, let me play, let Virgil Jones play a little bit

ctx.x: That’s right. And I never forgot that. And when I came off of that band and then started working with Bob Rosengarden’s band on “The Dick Cavett Show,” and that was a very professionally adept ensemble, I would have to say in the studios that was the most adept ensemble I have ever played with. I mean we had great players on there, I mean and they were just taking no prisoners. The band was so clean and so right, and what Rosengarden would do, bless him, is we would go into rehearsal and the first 45 minutes that…
Well he’s pretty astute to do something like that.
